inspected_frames.observation: Elongated tapering plated body, small attachment, eight spreading unbranched arms and small alternate projections read clearly.
Opposite arm gaps preserved; plain shallow upper surface has no invented deep opening or mouth/anus.
Conical elongated body and individual irregular plate facets; no columnal stalk or fivefold branched crown.
Arms remain separate and unbranched with small soft process cues; stalk/body reaches attachment without visible gap.
Thin integral plate/scalelike relief and several alternate processes visible; plate coloration is artistic.
Exactly eight arms with gaps, six small alternating processes per arm in actual geometry; not modern crinoid branching.
Plate facets and arm geometry remain without colors. Small protrusions genuinely three-dimensional.
Narrow attachment, broadening cone and unbranched crown retain intended outline.

supplementary_detail.observed_note: Individually viewed exact-subject additional detail; see final-detail-inspection and Arborea r003 record. Does not replace any of eight original full views.

concept_comparison: Retain irregular scale surfaces, elongated cone and unbranched arms. Concept has a conspicuous deep empty cup and arm count obscured: actual model closes the top with a shallow neutral surface without inventing mouth/anus, and has exactly eight separately readable arms. Plate relief restrained, not thick armored tiles; small soft processes alternate sides.
known_limitations: Whole animal inferred from fossils, with artistic pose/color and moderate low-poly plate relief. Affinity disputed between echinoderm and cnidarian interpretations; no categorical crinoid assignment, no mouth/anus or stereom modeled. ROM image collection attribution verified; GSC25962 separately verified in Ausich/Babcock1998 textfig1 and plate1. Substrate tube omitted as not part of the animal.
Color, thickness and idealized proportions are artistic except explicitly source-bounded hard ranges; no original specimen cast claim.
CPU stills and Node parsing are not actual GPU or composed-scene acceptance.
